title.narrative: BRAZIL BAHIA SUSTAINABLE RURAL DEVELOPMENT PROJECT

description.narrative: The Bahia Sustainable Rural Development Project for Brazil objectives are: to increase market integration, net revenues, and food security of organized beneficiaries; as well as to improve access to water supply and sanitation services of households in Project areas. The project consists of three components, the first on being the productive inclusion and access to markets will increase productive inclusion and access to markets for family farmers and other disadvantaged populations in the borrower?s territory. The second component is household water and sanitation that will support the borrower?s efforts to improve sanitation conditions and access to water supply services in the area where a pre-established adequate management system is present. The third component the institutional development, technical assistance and project management component will support the provision of technical assistance for carrying out necessary research and capacity building activities for technical staff. It will also provide support for the design and implementation of dissemination activities of the Project?s processes and results.
To increase market integration, net revenues, and food security of organized beneficiaries; as well as to improve access to water supply and sanitation services of households in Project areas.

Finance Agreement :Cooperation Agreement | Description :The Cooperation Agreement to be entered into between CAR and theCooperating Entity under terms and conditions acceptable to the Bank within sixty (60) days of the Declaration of Effectiveness,setting forth their respective roles and responsibilities regarding the implementation of the Project, for purposes of assistingCAR in the technical aspects of Project implementation. | Due Date :30-Nov-2014

Finance Agreement :Project Territorial Units | Description :The Borrower shall operate, and thereafter maintain until thecompletion of the Project, at least eighteen (18) Project TerritorialUnits under CAR for day-to-day Project implementation at thelocal level to ensure coordination and integration between local institutions and stakeholders in all 27 State Territories. |Frequency :CONTINUOUS

title.narrative: Increase in the total number of formal contracts integrating beneficiary Producer Organizations (POs) into markets

comment.narrative:
<p>Main target exceeded at 117.3%; and Female participation exceeded at 400.8%.</p>

<p>Achievements are detailed in Section IIB Efficacy. These indicators were measured based on the Business Plan annual monitoring survey, applied to the beneficiaries by Rural Community Agents (ACRs) and registered in the CARweb M&E system.  The figures for the final ISR were updated based on an actualized analysis at project completion which provided results only for (a) those subprojects which were completed by project closing; and (b) were implemented by POs under the Market-Oriented subproject strategy, as specified in the indicator definition.</p>

<p>Noe on revised targets:  Female participation target was reduced from 30% to 20% under the first restructuring (2017) to reflect the actual percentage of female-led Producer Organizations in the field, verified after the 1st Call for Expressions of Interest (CEI).</p>

<p>The three targets were exceeded: 107.8%  for the main indicator, 151.3% for female participation, and 204.5% for vulnerable populations.</p>

<p>Direct beneficiaries of Component 2 were informed by CERB based on the number of new (24,742) and recovered (5297) piped HH water connections. Total connections were multiplied by the IBGE coefficient of 3.41 (average inhabitants of occupied HH in Bahia). The number of women among total direct beneficiaries was calculated using the QAD applied up to 2020, which reported2% women. This percentage was then applied to the total number of beneficiaries, resulting in 43,124 women. The same approach was applied to calculate the vulnerable beneficiary population, with 51.2% in this category as of 2020.</p>

<p>Note on revised targets: The original targets were set based on the number of HH benefiting from new water connections (17,000) under Component 2, rather than the number of HH members.  The 1st Restructuring (May 2017) revised the target of 17,000 HH due to Comp 2 implementation delays which would affect the original projected number of beneficiaries.   The 2nd Restructuring (Feb 2021) increased the target to 28,000 HH because the component was well on track for implementation, the cost of each connection was lower than originally estimated, and exchange rate gains had made more funds available. The unit of measurement was also changed from HH to HH members - the number of HH was multiplied by the IBGE coefficient of 3.41, previously presented.  This resulted in a target of 95,000 direct beneficiaries under Comp 2 (28,000 HH x 3.41 persons per HH). (The same rationale was not followed fr Comp 1 which used the number of HH not HH members).</p>

<p>For the sub-indicators for women's participation and vulnerable populations benefiting under Comp 2, the intention was to set targets of 30% and 20% respectively. In the 1st Restructuring (2017), both sub-indicators were changed from percentages to numbers of people, maintaining the equivalent of 30% for female participation and increasing the number of vulnerable people from 20% to the equivalent of 28%.</p>

title.narrative: Increase in the real net revenue of beneficiary Rural Producer Organizations (RPOs)

comment.narrative:
<p>Main target was far exceeded at 1,290% and Female participation also far exceeded at 1,710%.</p>

<p>These indicators were measured based on the BP annual survey applied to the beneficiaries by Rural Community Agents (ACR) and registered in the CARweb M&E system.  Achievements are detailed in the Efficacy section.  The figures for the final ISR were updated based on an actualized analysis at project completion which provided results only for (a) those subprojects which were completed by project closing, and (b) were implemented by POs under the Market-Oriented subproject strategy, as specified in the indicator definition.</p>

<p>Note on revised targets: Female participation target numbers were not included in the approved PAD and were included in the 1st Resructuring (2017).</p>

title.narrative: Increase in the yearly volume of sales through contracts from beneficiary Producer Organizations (POs) and Community Associations (CAs).

comment.narrative:
<p>Target was far exceeded at 1,320%</p>

<p>This indicator was measured based on the annual Business Plan survey, applied to the beneficiaries by Rural Community Agents (ACR) and registered in the CARweb M&E system.</p>

<p>This indicator measures the increase in the annual monetary volume of sales but lacks information on the total number of production units. Therefore, considering that the main component of income is sales and that only taxes have been deducted to calculate net revenues, the result of this indicato is similar to PDO Indicator #2 and the information available does not permit a complementary analysis.</p>

<p>Note on revised targets: The 1st Restructuring (May 2017) revised the target numbers to reflect the time required to implement investments and start generating revenues for the PO. The end target was changed from 20% to 15%.</p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Increase in average vulnerable beneficiary household dietary diversity indicator

comment.narrative:
<p>Main target was partially achieved at 46.7% and Female participation partially achieved at 47.7%.</p>
<p>These indicators were measured based on a BP survey (Business Plan) applied by Rural Community Agents (ACR) only for the beneficiaries of CEI No. 1, Socio-Environmental, launched in 2015, CEI No. 11 Quilombola communities, and CEI No. 12 Indigenous communities., both launched in 2018. This indicator was calculated on the basis of IBGE composite indicator of minimum caloric intake requirements per family, as follows:  The sum of the total intake of food groups per household, where the food groups are: 1. Grains, 2. Roots and Tubers, 3. Vegetables, 4. Fruits, 5. Meat, Poultry, offal, 6. Eggs, 7. Fish and Seafood, 8. Pulses, Legumes, Nuts, 9. Milk and Milk Products, 10. Oils, Fats, 11. Sugar or Honey, 12. Miscellaneous (coffee, tea). The value of this variable would range from 0 to 12 for each household, and the average of the beneficiary household indicator was estimated for annual values. Achievements are detailed in the Efficacy section. </p>

title.narrative: Direct jobs generated as a result of the Project's interventions and investments - Component 2

comment.narrative:
<p>Target exceeded at 140%.</p>

<p>Indicator was measured by CERB, which provided monthly information to the CAR M&E Unit.</p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Direct jobs generated as a result of the Project's interventions and investments - Component 1

comment.narrative:
<p>Target far exceeded at 509%.</p>

<p>This indicator was measured based on information provided by the SACC system, which includes all staff hired to implement the investments.  This indicator was included by the 1st Restructuring to capture the number of jobs generated by the project, by Component.  It refers to jobs generated directly by the Rural Organizations and counting the number of rural community agents (ACR), construction inspectors, project designers, business and investment plan consultants, rural extension technical agents and management support technical assistants hired directly by organizations under Component 1.</p>

<p>Although most of these jobs were temporary, such as business plan consultants and construction inspectors, others such as the ACRs, the main contractors of the POs, were more permanent.  At the end of ACRs' contracts, a survey was conducted to understand to what extent the employment opportunities provided by the Project had been positive. Of the 281 respondents, 33% were working at the time of the survey, and 81% of them (the 281) continue to work in areas related to their ACR work, while a similar percentage inten to continue working in a similar area, even if some are not currently working.  In addition, for 99% of the ACRs consulted, their experience as an ACR helped/will help them find another job and contributed to their professional development.</p>

title.narrative: Market-oriented subproject beneficiaries who received training as a result of the Project

comment.narrative:
<p>Target was exceeded at 148.2%.</p>

<p>This indicator was measured using information provided on the SACC Capacitacao System, by the CAR Training Unit.</p>

<p>Between 2016 and 2022, the Project provided 445 courses on 21 different topics to 14,819 beneficiaries, including: 180 courses on 10 different topics focused on market-oriented subprojects for 8,323 beneficiaries; 69 courses on 4 topics for 2,368 beneficiaries of socio-environmental subprojects;  and 196 courses with 4,128 participants covering cross-cutting topics for both implementation strategies. The courses were also attended by project staff and other stakeholders (see Table, Annex 7).</p>

<p>Note on revised targets:  This indicator was added by the 1st Restructuring (2017) to capture how many beneficiaries of market-oriented subprojects would benefit from project training. The indicator reflects the total number of subproject beneficiaries, market-oriented and socio-environmental, completed and under implementation/completion, trained by the Project.</p>

title.narrative: Basic WSS investments implemented and sustainably operated

comment.narrative:
<p>Target exceeded at 140%.</p>

<p>This indicator was measured by CERB, which provided monthly information to CAR's M&E Unit. The indicator provides information on completed investments of sustainably implemented and operated basic WSS systems with (a) voluntary adherence to a management plan; and (b) timely payments to management units for the service.</p>

<p>Note on revised targets:  The PAD estimated an average of 100 HH per each WSS system. Therefore, a target of 170 WSS systems was set to reach the initially estimated 17,000 HH. During the 1st Restructuring (2017) the target was revised to reflect delays in the implementation of Comp 2 that would affect the final number.  The end target was changed from 170 to 125. However, the 2nd Restructuring (2021) did not adjust the target when the number of water connections was increased to 23,000.</p>

<p>Main target was partially achieved at 52.0%; Female participation and share of Vulnerable People were exceeded at 111.7% and 100.4% respectively.</p>

<p>It is important to note that the indicator was calculated based on the subprojects completed.  If incomplete subprojects were also considered, for a total of 1,169 subprojects, the results would be as follows:  Main indicator exceeded at 113.2% with 38,783 beneficiaries (88% of the 39,000 target - See note on revised targets below); Female participation far exceeded at 232.3% with 23, 865 women, and Vulnerable Populations far exceeded at 218.6% with 21,718 people receiving Bolsa Familia benefits within this cohort.</p>

<p>The direct beneficiaries of Component 1 were reported based on the number of households declared by rural organizations (PO and CA) in the awarded CEI.  Female participation is based on the number of households headed by women that were informed when the contracts were signed with the rural organizations. The vulnerable population was calculated based on the households headed by people registered in the Unified Registry for Social Programs (Cadastro Unico para Programas Sociais or CadUnico) which seeks to identify all low-income families in the country to include them in social assistance programs such as "Bolsa Familia".</p>

<p>Note on revised targets: (a) The target for this indicator refers to direct beneficiaries, and was set based on the number of households (HH) benefiting from the project, not household members. The 1st Restructuring revised the overall target of 56,000 beneficiaries (39,000 Comp 1 and 17,000 Comp 2) because of implementation delays in Component 2 water investments affecting the number of beneficiaries. End target for total beneficiaries was changed from 56,000 to0,000, but there was an error of calculation. Beneficiary HH under Comp 2 changed from 17,000 to 8,000 so total beneficiaries should have been reduced to 47,000 (39,000 Comp 1, 8,000 Comp 2). (b) The intention was to set targets of 20% and 30% respectively for women and vulnerable populations (VP). Also, the sub-indicator for VP changed the unit of measurement from percentage to number and increased the target to 11,200 or about 28%. (c) The 2nd Restructuring split the indicator by Component and revised the target numbers. Target for Comp 1 continued to be HH but was changed to persons for Comp 2. The change in the target number from 39,000 to 34,250 HH in Comp 1 is unexplained. The Restructuring Paper mentioned 1,250 subprojects for Comp 1 under implementation instead of the 400 originally planned. However, the target target was not increased to match the increase in the number of subprojects. The Project achieved 88% of the original 39,000 target for Comp 1.</p>

title.narrative: Direct jobs generated as a result of the Project's interventions and investments - Component 3

comment.narrative:
<p>Target exceeded at 109%.</p>

<p>This indicator was measured based on the information provided by FLEM (see previous indicator).</p>

<p>Note on revised targets:  This indicator was included by the 1st Restructuring (2017) to capture the number of jobs generated by the Project under Comp 3.  The 240 direct jobs comprise 127 PMU technical staff, 102 Rural Extension Technical Agents hired by the ATER provider, and 11 Consultants.</p>

title.narrative: New piped household water connections that are resulting from the project intervention

comment.narrative:
<p>Main target exceeded at 107.6% and Female participation far exceeded at 473.3%.</p>

<p>The main indicator was measured by CERB, which provided monthly information to CAR's M&E unit.  The indicator provides information on new, piped, household watr connections where construction work has been completed and the connections are operational.  Female participation was measured by the Territorial Approach Questionnaire (QAD), applied by the CERB Social Unit in all the locations served.  Details on the achievements can be seen in the Efficacy section IIB.  At project closing, the civil works for 26, 390 household water connections had been completed, but 1,648 were not yet operational.  The figure of 71% refers to the percentage of female-led households surveyed by QAD in the early years of the Project up to March 2020, after which this percentage was projected for subsequent years.</p>

<p>Note on revised targets:  The target of 350 new piped households in the original Results Framework was incorrect. According to the PAD narrative, it should have been 17,000. Due to delayed implementation of Component 2, the target was adjusted to 8,000 households under the 1st Restructuring (2017).  In the 2nd Restructuring (2021), the target was increased again to 23,000 households because the Component was well on track for implementation, the cost per connection was lower than originally estimated, and exchange rate gains had made more funds available. The final target for Female participation was changed from 30% to 15%, based on the actual number of female-led households at the time of the 1st Restructuring (2017).</p>

title.narrative: Number of people benefitting from capacity building on management of water supply and sanitation systems

comment.narrative:
<p>Main target far exceeded at 12,867% and Female participation similarly exceeded at 11,666%.</p>

<p>These indicators were measured by CERB, which provided monthly data to CAR's M&E Unit. The main source of data was the attendance lists of training activities/events.</p>

<p>The Project carried out a remarkable social work effort in the communities served by the 3 Centrais (Jacobina, Seabra, Caetite), contributing to the gradual acceptance of the Central model by the communities. During implementation, the need to sensitize and raise awareness in the beneficiary communities about the importance of charging for water use was recognized to ensure sustainability of the model.  For this reason, it was decided to train as many beneficiaries as possible, in addition to operators of the systems.</p>

<p>Note on revised targets:  The 1st Restructuring adjusted the targets in line with delays in implementation of Comp 2. End target changed from 340 to 250. Regarding the gender sub-indicator, the narrative explained that the target was reduced to from 30% to 15% of women, however the target continued to reflect 30% of the total number of people. End target changed from 102 to 75 (30% of 250).</p>

title.narrative: People trained to improve hygiene behavior/sanitation practices under the proj

comment.narrative:
<p>Main target far exceeded at 374.3% and sub-indicator of Female participation also far exceeded at 375%.</p>

<p>These indicators were measured by CERB which provided monthly information to CAR's M&E Unit. The indicators provide information on trainingctivities to improve hygiene behavior or sanitation practices among beneficiaries and were measured through the attendance lists of training activities. The training activities were conducted in 100% of the communities benefiting from the WSS systems. The tagets were far exceeded due to the use of virtual training during the COVID-19 pandemic, which allowed the project to reach a higher number of participants than planned.  CERB conducted a Healthy Habits Monitoring Survey in the catchment areas of the Seabra ad Jacobina Centrais, which showed the adoption and maintenance of healthy habits over time, before and after the training and the receipt of project benefits. Results showed positive changes in families' habits of washing hands before meals, after using the toilet, personal cleanliness, rational use of water, and use of the toilet and its components.</p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Number of government staff and strategic partners trained in accordance with the Project Capacity Building Plan

comment.narrative:
<p>Main target was Substantially achieved at 91.6% and Female participation was exceeded at 132.1%.</p>

<p>This indicator was measured based on the information provided by FLEM (Fundacao Luis Eduardo Magalhaes), a Cooperation Institution with international technical expertise, contracted to expand and strengthen CAR's technical and operational capacity. The Project reported that it covered all the training demand from government staff and strategic partners, so the target number was likely over-estimated.</p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Producer Organizations (POs) and Community Associations (CAs) implementing financial management instruments in subprojects

comment.narrative:
<p>Main target exceeded at 136.3% and Female participation exceeded at 179.2%.</p>

<p>Indicators were measured based on the Business Plan annual survey applied by the ACRs and registered in CARweb, the M&E system.  Out of 590 completed subprojects, 92.4% (545) used financial management tools in their subprojects, of which 215 (39%) were led by women. The database also provides information on the types of financial management tools used by organizations: 68% used basic accounting controls; 13% profit and loss statement; 8% used balance sheets; and 5% used sales forecasts. Most organizations used just basic accounting tools and there is much room for improvement to strengthen organizations in this area.</p>

<p>Note on revised targets: In the PAD, these indicators had the same targets as indicators related to business and investment plans implemented (750), since it was expected that all POs benefiting from a subproject would implement financial management tools. Thus, the 1st Restructuring (May 2017) revised targets in the same way. Target for main indicator was reduced from 750 to 400 rural organizations, and for the gender indicator from 225 to 120. The target was exceeded because the Project significantly increased the number of subprojects but the targets were not updated.</p>

title.narrative: Number of business plans & investment plans implemented by POs and CAs

comment.narrative:
<p>Main target exceeded at 175% and Female led POs and CAs far exceeded at 199.2%.</p>

<p>These indicators were measured based on the information registered in CARweb, the M&E system at closing.</p>

<p>Some 469 subprojects are at various stages of completion as at ICR finalization. If the total of 1,169 fully and partly implemented subprojects is applied, and the percentage is estimated for 434 women-led POs and CAs within the 1,169, the indicator results would be 292.3% and 193%, respectively.</p>

<p>Note on revised targets:  The 1st Restructuring (May 2017) reduced final targets from 750 to 400 for the main indicator and from 225 to 120 for the gender sub-indicator due to delays in implementing the BPs and investment plans in the project's early years, which was not going to permit completions as originally planned. These indicators should have been revised upward by the 2nd Restructuring (Feb 2021) when a 22-month extension was approved and some 1,250 subprojects were being implemented (final number 1,169). </p>

title.narrative: Clients who have adopted an improved agr. technology promoted by the project

comment.narrative:
<p>Main target exceeded at 109.6% and Female participation far exceeded at 215.2%.</p>

<p>These indicators were informed by the Value Chain Production Specialists to the M&E Unit.</p>

<p>The improved agricultural technologies were measured in 154 rural organizations, out of a total 1,169 in the following value chains: Sheep/Goat, Cassava, Oilseeds and Fruit Farming. The impact evaluation provided information on producers' perceptions on the adoption of the improved agricultural technologies and the ease of putting it into practice. More than 47% of respondents considered it easy or very easy, 6.8% considered it complicated and only 1% saw it as very complicated.</p>

<p>Note on revised targets:  The original targets were for 550 (73%) of the 750 planned subprojects to adopt improved agricultural technologies and for 165 of the 225 women-led rural organizations.  The 1st Restructuring revised targets to account for the results of the first CEI and the fact that an improved agricultural technology can be promoted by CAR but has to be requested by the potential beneficiary.  Targets were changed from 550 to 400 for the main indicator and from 165 to 120 for the gender sub-indicator.  In the 2nd Restructuring (Feb 2021), the intention was to increase the targetso better reflect the large number of approved subprojects.  However, the definition of "clients who adopted an improved technology" was changed by replacing rural organization (PO and CA) with individuals, thus increasing the target number to 7,000 persons. </p>

title.narrative: People provided with access to "improved sanitation facilities under the proj.

comment.narrative:
<p>Main target exceeded at 108.4% and Female participation far exceeded at 473.3%.</p>

<p>The main indicator was measured by CERB, which provided monthly information to CAR's M&E Unit.   Female participation was collected through the Territoria Approach Questionnaire (QAD) applied in all the localities served by the CERB Social Unit. The figure of 71% refers to the percentage of female-led households surveyed by QAD in the early years of the project up to March 2020 after which this percentage was projected for subsequent years. The 8,675 beneficiaries represent the 2,544 households that received improved sanitation facilities of which 1,806 (71%) were female-led households.</p>

<p>Note on revised targets:  The original target of 17,000 was based on the number of new piped water connections to households. Despite the reference to "people" in the definition, it can be iferred that the unit of measure for this indicator was households.  In the 1st Restructuring (2017), the target was adjusted to 8,000 people to account for the reduction in new water connections defined in the previous indicator.  In the 2nd Restructuring, the target was not adjusted to the number of new household connections, as a diagnosis conducted in the project intervention areas revealed that the need for new sanitation facilities was much lower than initially estimated. Although it seems clear that the indicator referred to the number of households, it was measured in terms of people receiving sanitation facilities as defined. Even so, the demand for improved sanitation facilities was fully met.</p>

<p>The final target for female participation was changed from 30% to 15%, based on the actual number of female-led households at the time of the 1st Restructuring. The original unit of measurement was people, which changed to percentage of people in the 2nd Restructuring (2021).</p>

<p> </p>

title.narrative: Targeted clients satisfied with agricultural services (percentage)

comment.narrative:
<p>Main target exceeded at 120.3%, male beneficiaries at 116.1%, and female beneficiaries at 121.2%.</p>

<p>These indicators were measured based on the technical assistance beneficiary satisfaction questionnaires applied by the Business Plan Coordination of Technical Assistance and Rural Extension (ATER).</p>

<p>The questionnaires were applied annually to a sample of beneficiary organizations (135) to assess the quality of services and serve as a basis for their improvement, in addition to renewing the services of the companies providing TA services.  The service is considered satisfactory when the  beneficiary gives a score greater than or equal to 7 on a scale of 1 to 10.  ATER services played a key role in Component 1. Main objective was to improve sustainable production and manufacturing practices, promote new practices, and introduce technologies that would increase productivity and economic results, reduce agricultural risks, improve organization and planning to transform the family production unit into a sustainable business, ensure quality production, regularity of supply, and scale, and generate an economic and social return for the supported families. See Appendix to Annex 7 on the Project's ATER services.</p>

<p>Note on revised targets:  The 1st Restructuring (2017) dropped the original indicator and created a new indicator to correctly measure percentages rather than total numbers of target clients.</p>

<p>Main target exceeded at 106% and Female participation was far exceeded at 473.3%</p>

<p>The main indicator was measured by CERB which sent the information monthly to CAR's M&E Unit. The indicator provides information on household water connections recvered, where construction work has been completed and the service is operational. Female participation was measured by the QAD which was applied by the CERB Social Unit in all the localities served.  Achievements are detailed in the Efficacy section IIB.</p>

<p>Note on revised targets:  This indicator was added by the 2nd Restructuring (2021) to reflect the additonal investments included in the Project for rehabilitation of existing water supply systems.</p>

<p> </p>
